text:
I frail grey man appeared on the trail ahead.
I cocked my head up towards ARC9.
"Scan does not register. I suggest caution." he said.
Curiosity may have killed the cat, but not this dog.
With a generous wag I urged us forward

Sandy cared little for the noble breeds. They lacked cunning and were easily misled. The trust of a street dog; however, was worth more than a freshly pinched rib-eye. Jack knew this too. They circled. How hard to fight? More than pain they feared losing a new friend

As the thief escaped into the woods, Sandy barked him towards Wilson's point. There he waited for hunger to set in. When men get hungry they get reckless. Street dogs get focused.
5 am, with the scythe moon receding...
      "Ill get you, you mongr—"

Sandy and ARC9 paused their pursuit at a lazy stone wall once a cue to farmers and cows. ARC9 considered defunct ordinances; Sandy the scent of fox and wolves. The tracks ambled north to the thicket of pine hiding the missing child and his pile of candy wrappers

A clue led Sandy and ARC9 to a chain of islands reachable only by boat. The crossing's sea air stirred distant fears in the street dog. The robot's worries: corrosion.  At the pier, worry turned to action - find the smuggler's cave and hopefully a litter of puppies

Sandy imagined an afternoon asleep in the park dreaming of squirrels.  He would wait with ARC9 for another clue.
No sooner had his paws squared to the sun, the robot chirped "Suspect at Sola Park"
Sandy turned an ear.
     "No, dogs still can not ride the Cyclone"

The old texts left out details should they fall into enemy hands. ARC9 had ore, water, nuclear power... but failed to judge wind and soon was covered in soot, smelting iron. Sandy grinned: buy a sword?
  "Tomorrow, I temper steel"
The street dog sighed. Who is stubborn?

ARC9 intently watched Sandy dream- running, tail erect, whimpers. The street dog did not whimper when hunting, so he must be trying to escape? The robot dutifully recorded the timing of each start, stop and turn, mapping to city grids, hoping to unlock Sandy's past

From high upon the bluff the beach looked like an arm flexing muscles: smooth sandy skin leading to a curled forearm extending out into the bay; the boardwalk a tattoo upon the  bicep.  Sandy and ARC9 began the hike down to question both denizen and food truck

They entered the harbor north of Watson's Bay, came past the Opera House and settled at Circular Quay. While ARC9 eagerly scanned the jugglers and men on stilts, Sandy lamented his coat. When passing the equator winter had become summer.  He could not shed fast enough

DNA testing could establish lineage in purebreds, but not in street dogs. "We are all golden" some would say. And it was true. And all terrier, hound and shepherd. Sandy did not care to know his makeup. He was his own dog. ARC9, who found him quite unpredictable, agreed

The alley behind the dollar store reeked of garbage, spilled beer and urine. Mikey, Spike, Lady — all to be expected, but a foreign scent as well. A younger Sandy would have sought a fight, but with a job to do, he and ARC9 slipped into the shadows to observe.
Owooo

Joe did not grok Alex's disco music or veganism. He did, however, trust her bs detector. When the TV spat "victory imminent" and she spat her tofu, he knew the war was just beginning.
   "Alex find that reporter"
    "Already pinged ARC9, boss"
    "of course you did"

Anger, distrust and hope colored the crowd assembled at the doc. ARC9 growled into the mic "We regret to inform you reparations are not possible only relocation"
  "And the fish?"
  "Enough for sustainable diversity"
Quickly, Sandy barked the Polar Bears on to the ship

A gash in the barbed-wire fence highlighted the duo's idealogical differences. Curious by nature, Sandy darted through the hole while compliant ARC9 stayed put. The robot was the street dog's protector, however. ARC9 concluded guarding the retreat would logically suffice
Surprisingly the cave was empty. ARC9 concealed his disappointment behind a steel facade. Sandy’s crestfallen tail was harder to hide
A hard day on the trails had left the duo in knots.  ARC9 needed WD40, but what about the street dog? ARC9 was fresh out of plush toys for vivisection... perhaps beach therapy?

If escaping meant leaving nurse Lola behind, Serious P had no interest in freedom. Sandy and ARC9 considered options.
   "No we can't kidnap her" chirped the robot.
Sandy sighed, then pawed the robot twice.
   "Yes, maybe she could take you for a walk. A very long walk"

the robot guarded
his refined deuterium
the street dog, rib-eyes. haiku

Sandy had met Argo behind Prospect hill. His ears were good, eyes fair, nose elite; perhaps beyond elite.  The street dog reckoned he could be a good ally. Sandy also welcomed the companionship, but not all the time lost to p-mail
ARC9 shook the whipped cream can vigorously.  Sandy sighed.  Another clear example of the robot's far too literal interpretations.   The party was not until tomorrow

ARC9 knew fear; not his own - but his companion Sandy's.  It took the robot many years to learn them, however, for the normal street dog fears were not Sandy's.  He did not fear Man. He did not fear cars, guns or hunger. Sandy was afraid of ceiling fans

"Robot you ain't known the pleasure of a woman's touch, or that feelin' when she looks at you just so"
ARC9 blinked.
 "Or when she helps you up after a fall" Serious P continued.
The robot turned. "We must rescue her"
 "And her cookin'"
Sandy's tail vigorously approved

Having a robot companion had its advantages: language translation, lugging supplies, credits, welding torch...; but sometimes Sandy did miss living alone. Scaring hot-dog vendors... chasing poodles for no reason... Also, ARC9 disapproved leaving p-mail on monuments

“Lola you have beautiful eyes”
“Serious, what do you want?”
“What do you mean?”
“You trying to butter me up. You want something”
“Let’s run away”
“You know i can’t”
“Pecan pie?”
ARC9’s circuit flipped. “Sandy let’s go. He needs our help”
The duo barged through the door
The classic phrase summed up the duo’s differences perfectly. ARC9 sought permission, Sandy forgiveness. Well it was mostly true. ARC9 did seek permission

From across the street Sandy watched the groomer with suspicion — a boxer shampooed,  doodle bids farewell to winter coat... ARC9 assured him the visit was necessary. Something about a "dog smell."

Sandy wasn't buying it.  He had the superior nose after all

Serious P was on a roll. "It ain't no coincidence. Damn shifts lead to more daddy hacks and more strikeouts. Killing the game. Gotta outlaw it."
Sandy, also a traditionalist, nodded.
  "...and don't get me started on robot umpires!"
ARC9 blinked. Let's not get personal

Serious P carried on. "There are some dumb-ass people out there. What they pay for 'art' makes me cry."
The duo tried to ignore him.
  "I mean, 120K for a banana! What?"
Sandy had to nod.  He did not like bananas either.
ARC9 added "Someone did eat it."

The Oak and Main hydrant p-mail caught Sandy's attention. Why was Hunter this far north when he'd been barking up plans to prowl Karl's point? Was the barking a decoy?
  "Maybe he is lost" offered ARC9.
A strong possibility agreed Sandy. Hunter was a house-dog after all

Sandy’s relationship with fear was forged in his earliest days as a street dog. He did not scare easily, but when scared it went deep. Sandy also learned how to scare— ears pinned back, tail down, teeth bared… his quick sharp bark could petrify the largest of men

Serious P was out cold suffering from sun stroke or perhaps too much gin. Either way they needed to keep moving.
  "ARC9 how do we revive him?" asked Alex.
Sandy raised a paw.
  "Yes?" the robot inquired.
Sandy hearing an answer, not a question, unleashed his wet tongue

Sirius P looked the color that only a night of too much tequila could produce.
 “something to pacify your stomach?” Alex offered, handing him some water.
 “no mam. hair of the dog that bit me”
This got Sandy’s attention. And he promptly fetched the Patron

Alex and Serious P had hit a snag. "You can't expect me to remember the details the same every time. It's not like I pay attention"
Alex knew this. All the same she needed facts.
Sandy set out to mend the relationship.
Common enemy... muddy brook... Shake, shake, shake!

Early one morning the sun was shining. A red haired woman approached.
 "Can you help me out of a jam?"
ARC9 scanned the lines of her face.
 "You are married to a carpenter"
  "Soon to be divorced"
Serious P sat up. "Don't I know your name?"
And that's how it all started

Sandy had lost Hunter's scent. Begrudgingly he pawed ARC9 and pointed to a string of crows perched above. The robot dutifully chirped, whistled and beeped.
After some thought the birds replied a single high-pitch note
Alex asked "What did they say?"
 "3 miles north shed"

“The paper will need a photo, Sandy” Alex insisted.
But the street dog, a portrait of stubbornness, would have none of it.  Photos steal your sole. He skirted into the brush, ostensibly chasing a squirrel.
 “Don’t worry” ARC9 assured her “I have footage”

ARC9’s plan had been clear. Sandy sniff the hydrant on Oak, the lamp at Shaw’s, return to the green at 7 avoiding Main. The robot would scan the south side. Where was Sandy?

As the church bell rang 6 ARC9 knew the flaw. Neither the street dog nor Father Tom groked DST

An errant lightening bolt had left ARC9's blinker fritzed. Sandy did not care for he had been avoiding the robot anyway, but Alex was stressed. As If the robot's incessant literalism was not bad enough she now had to contend with an infinite stare.
 "Sandy, fetch!"
Woof!

“you were a shock jock?” alex asked with a raised brow.
“indeed” Serious P reflected. “or maybe better said, a ‘truth teller’”
Sandy snored. ARC9 blinked.
“i think thats why i was picked” he continued.
“to toe their lie?”
“exactly”

Sandy takes a second sniff then darts quickly through the unlatched fence. The fox scent might fool a house dog, but it’s clearly a mock. The quantity alone, requiring no less than 100 fox, a dead giveaway.

He then pauses lifting his head. What’s that drumming sound?

After 100 days (of VS365!!!), Sandy and ARC9 took a pause from solving mysteries to reflect upon what they had accomplished and ponder what the future held in store. More adventures with the nonsensical Serious P...?

ARC9 blinked as the street dog darted off to find out

there once was a street dog from the city
whose first year was often not pretty
if lore had it right
he’d learned how to fight
‘fore gettin’ weened from the

Sandy preferred run down Horn park at the old school to Center park, and surely would never venture to the gated Heights park with its house dogs and cappuccinos.
 "C'mon" prodded Serious P. "Plenty to be learned in enemy territory"
The street dog sniffed for more data

ARC9 read the dispatch aloud: 5 houses burgled on North street between 8 and 11 AM; doors and windows smashed.

With a stretch Sandy accordioned up out of the long grass and started towards the park entrance. If nothing else there would be house dogs to round up

Sandy passed hydrants and lampposts overdue for a visit, ARC9 pushing the street dog hard. He would need to carve out time for p-mail later.
Cresting the hill at High street they saw the ferry boarding below.
 “tchk tchk” the robot clicked.
Time to pick up the pace

Sandy dreamt in a prior life he had been an eagle, living high in the crags, swooping down to best gulls for unguarded hotdogs and pretzels at the boardwalk.  He imagined ARC9 had been a stop sign.  The robot still new to this line of inquiry, said "No, I was an ATM"

In the wild house dogs are reckless. Soft, slow and reckless. Hunter was no exception and needed to be rounded up before he caused more trouble.
ARC9 agreed with the plan but considered Sandy's intolerance equally brash

Sandy traced a bluestone path from the estate down to a turquoise kidney-shaped pool reminiscent of a 1960's Les Paul. Each stone in the path had pearl inlay and an ivory fret. He understood why a dog would live here. The cat in the window would need to go, however

An earthquake caught Sandy and ARC9 off guard tumbling the robot to the ground, a rivulet of grey now seeping from his neck. The street dog lifted his nose.
 “Don’t fret Sandy -zzzrt- repair the coolant -grrg- town.”
The liquid did not smell like antifreeze

Sending p-mail takes practiced aim taking into account wind, rain, uneven surfaces and that you are frequently facing the opposite direction. Sandy did practice (a lot) and considered himself an excellent writer.

ARC9 reminds him that quality not quantity matters most

The Riverton marching band struggled mightily against a crepuscular concert of mosquitos, crickets and bats. ARC9 took this as foreshadowing of the team’s upcoming troubles and suggested seeking friday night fun elsewhere. Sandy agreed, snagging a hot dog before leaving

Sandy hopped up onto the sea wall, baiting the  rottweiler further. What next? The street dog mulled his options… A whimper should do the trick.

Lips back, the rotty charged.

Sandy hit him with the old stutter step. 100 lbs of drool sailed past into the water below

(cue orchestra)
-The afternoon sun at High park gently warms a street dog and robot lounging in tall grass. Birds chirp.
-A giant shadow descends threatening to destroy paradise
(dun Dun DUNH)
-A cloud
-The street dog resumes dream of stealing steaks from BBQ picnic

The carriage path ended at a stone wall abutting an overgrown cemetery. Sandy approached quickly keen to jump the wall and play amongst the headstones and wild flowers. At the last moment, however, he abruptly stopped. A distant voice warned of Carson the Cruel

Sandy worked his way off the pier, back behind town hall, through the university fields and up the hill to High park.  Unless he could get clear of the parade crowds he would not be able to wind down.
ARC9 suggested medication.
Sandy agreed the robot needed some

Sandy's stomach churned for steak. Alas none could be found in High park with BBQ season now over. Heading to town seemed like a chore as did chasing hare. Being hungry seemed like the only option.
ARC9 reminded him dandelion greens were nutritious.
He'd rather be hungry

Working south along the coast under the moon’s light the duo came upon a seal absently crooning like a blackbird.
“i have rescued a ball. has a child lost one?” ARC9 translated.
Tomorrow would be joyous, Sandy thought, as the seal handed him the ball

The Smith's front yard was an embarrassment of kitsch- scarecrow, wheel barrow full of hay, six pink flamingos and an animatronic heron requesting you have a nice day. Sandy avoided the house- especially the picket fence gossip p-mail.
ARC9 had sympathy for the heron

Unlike most street dogs, Sandy was at ease in the woods. The fresh air, clean mud, abundance of squirrels to chase all put a spring in his step. And no cars. He had been quilled by a porcupine so not everything was perfect, but in balance all good.
ARC9 kept bears away

Through the mansion's majestic front window, Sandy caught sight of his old mentor Kurt asleep on an oriental rug. Heart racing, his mind a tangle of fear, sorrow, envy and love, the street dog froze. What had happened to the cunning hound?
ARC9 knocked on the door

Sandy holed up in High Park after a day of excess- the rib eye variety. He had consumed a lot of water as well and now needed to sleep it off.
The next morning, refreshed, he left a river of p-mail bragging of his exploits.
ARC9 was not impressed

Fireworks over, Sandy began the descent into town snaking the crowd's ebb keeping his head down. Out of his left eye he spotted a turquoise suit with a folded pink scarf. And with a blink of the same eye the suit vanished.
Sandy gulped.
Had the League of Flowers returned?

Alex turned to ARC9 “What does he think is more fun, fetch or tug-of-war?”
What kind of question is that, snorted Sandy. That is like asking: which is better surf or turf? Both obviously.
ARC9 answered the reporter’s question thoughtfully “Both”

Good boy smiled Sandy

Resting between yesterday and tomorrow an old turtle had stopped on Rt 8, holding a line of cars (now twenty two long) at bay.
ARC9 approached her slowly for she was a snapper. “Do you need any help?”
 “Oh no” she laughed, glancing at the cars. “I like messin’ with em”

Sandy yawned. House dogs barking on Oak St was not signal of wolf. Why bother?
ARC9 gave him a gentle prod. "Short-wave indicates the stranger in turquoise has returned"
Sandy sat up quickly shaking of his malaise.
Why didn't you say so first?
The robot blinked patiently

Sandy agreed to neighborhood watch with ARC9. He had sensed trouble or maybe it was the full moon.
At midnight a scream burst from the Governor's house. Sandy did not hesitate darting through the open front door.
"Fluffy escaped!"
ARC9 blinked. This would not end well

Tourist dogs, with their leashes, obedience and sunscreened humans, congregated at the bowl in front of Meg’s Seaside Cafe. Sandy too was thirsty and his patience was ebbing.

Fortunately ARC9 noticed Meg had left a bowl for her favorite street dog in the alley out back

The cult huddled on the beach, high-fived, then slowly separated, forming a ring. Circling, they raised their hands again, shrieked and ran to the sea.
 “What does that bit signify?” Alex whispered.
 “Crashing to earth” ARC9 suggested.
Sandy thought they liked swimming

Was it innocence or naïveté? Did it matter? Sandy darted across Prince St and grabbed the lost puppy by the scruff of the neck. He would bring it back to High park and teach it some common sense.

Unbeknownst to the street dog, ARC9 also scanned for adoption homes

33 Oak had been vacant for years. One rumor was a ghost lived there that scared people away but that was false. In fact the house did not radiate evil at all. Buyers somehow just knew the house preferred to be alone.
It did enjoy visits from a worldly street dog however

From High Park ARC9 scanned the accident scene—three cars, ice cream truck, elephant, two mimes reenacting "who's on first?", juggler on stilts, children hypnotized.
Something was wrong.
The robot paused, calculating.
"Sandy, wait!"
The cars were too small

Strength helped set the pecking order of the north point street dogs, but cunning was critical for maintaining. Sandy tired of the struggle, a year of outsmarting a treacherous third, the constant nipping at his heels and set out on his own.
ARC9 was a fine companion

Sandy and ARC9 flee the congested rally only to find high park also overrun with people. The robot suggests continuing to the suburbs calculating suburbanites were at the rally.
What about house dogs?
Sandy instead enters caves north of the park.
ARC9 cautiously follows

Sandy tiptoed past the chicken coop, pig trough and sleeping cow trying desperately not to spook any of farmer John’s animals. It was late and a ruckus might also wake John’s shotgun.
ARC9 wondered about unnecessary risks.
The street dog smelled pie

ARC9’s inscape could best be described by Gödel’s most famous theorem. But which side of the coin did he occupy—incomplete or inconsistent? The robot could only speculate…

Sandy suggested “both.”

ARC9, lights-off, supposedly de-fragging, rose up straight and began to sleepwalk across the room. Sandy had seen many somnambulists before, but this was entirely new. Were the robot's sensors active?  Only one way to find out. Sandy gave a skateboard a good push

a little scout lore for your friday.
—

ARC9 could not compute why the campfire smoke never blew towards Sandy.  The street dog knew, of course. He hated cats

Miraculously the skateboard glided right between the robot's legs.
ARC9 then continued sleepwalking, expertly avoiding an ottoman, a pair of wicker rocking chairs and a lamp shaped like the Eiffel tower. Sandy could not sugarcoat it. The robot led a charmed life

The fingerprint on ARC9’s visor was a mystery. Neither the robot nor street dog had seen or heard anyone enter the room last night. Sandy jumped his paws up on the robot’s chest to investigate further. What was that smell? Perfume? Was that a hint of lipstick?

A CX11 droid slumped in the corner, eyes primrose, ochre coolant seeping from a gashed helmet. A safe also lay demolished, door violently separated from its housing. Had the droid been guard or unlucky thief? ARC9 assumed thief.
Sandy sniffed the empty safe for clues

the street dog saga-
guns, knives, saving lives,
cars, trucks, wayward ducks,
gangs on choppers, helicopters,
house dogs, cats, winter hats,
and tourists.
When Sandy was done wagging his own tail he looked up at ARC9 who chirped “and robots”

Sandy gazed at a BBQ across the park. He had not had a steak in weeks. If ARC9 could sound an alarm the coast would be clear.
ARC9 also chirped in a hypothetical. "If I were to acquire you a steak would you go to the groomers?"
Sandy groaned.
A street dog has standards

Knowing Sandy could benefit from a blind eye, ARC9 occasionally accepted jobs with local PD. Sandy understood the game and usually played along.
Clearing out North St tested his resolve, however. He had caused trouble there in his day. Maybe there was another way

The chase was on! Sandy darted up a gravel path through a gathering of trees into the park. Picking up speed he bounded into the tall grass his tail a golden plume surfing the green sea.
Sandy stopped to let the rabbit catch up. You go first now he waved with his paw

Autumn’s colder neighbor arrived early causing commotion among squirrels, chipmunks and hanger-on leaves. Sandy wasn’t happy either, his winter coat still in storage. But ARC9 assured him this was only a visit.  The street dog was less certain with the geese moving out

ARC9’s first year with Sandy would normalize many things the robot had been programmed to prevent— j-walking, digging holes in the governor’s yard, sleeping during the day… The street dog was not always the best role model, but he did have a good heart
ARC9 did not understand shame, most mistakes being logical miscalculations. Misjudging Sandy’s recent tolerance of house dogs however stumped the robot. Apparently old dogs can learn new tricks?

The constable did not consult with ARC9 before showing Sandy the April Lane photos. Predictably the street dog turned and sprinted from the station before a plan could be set.
 "Robot?"
 "He sheltered at that soup kitchen for six months"
 "oh"
 "We need to go Constable"

“What kind of dog is Sandy?”
ARC9 carefully considered the reporter’s question before answering.
What breed?
Temperament?
Function?
Origin?
The robot blinked twice, then looked down at the street dog.
“Companion”

Sandy’s philosophy nap contemplated when “do what you love” and “help others” conflict. Tabby the house cat was stuck in a tree. Maybe he had chased her there? Maybe he should fetch ARC9?
Wind began to tickle his nose…
A younger Sandy would wait.
Woof Woof

ARC9 repeated the police dispatch one more time “man shot spouse missing”
Sandy scowled still not sure who they were looking for. The robot agreed punctuation would have been helpful

Sandy was proud but knew excessive pride was a vulnerability. So he frequently sought opportunities to test his modesty. Cornering a skunk behind Fink's tavern was such an opportunity.
ARC9 intervened "You may not care but I do"
The street dog paused. Was mercy weakness?

The duo followed the tracks to a small log cabin, empty save a wooden table and chair, the remnants of a frugal lunch and a felt hat covering a worn leather journal.
ARC9 scanned the last entry, alas, not finding “rob governor’s house.”
Sandy sniffed the lunch for clues

Sandy rested peacefully heaving deep breaths into the crisp November evening. ARC9 kept a watchful eye.
Just when the robot had begun to worry the tryptophan nap had gone on too long, Sandy abruptly woke from his dream.
“No you did not miss pie” HappyThanksgiving

Finding a few quick barks insufficient, Sandy rose, trotted briskly across the pier to nip Hunter in the ear, steering him away from the girls in heat.  Hunter was full grown, but clearly nobody had giving the house dog “the conversation”

Somewhat hypocritically Sandy bristled at ARC9’s blatant rule breaking. It was still November yet the robot had switched his LEDs to green and red.
Sensing trouble ARC9 chirped “Don’t worry, I won’t start carols until next week”
Sandy backed down, crisis averted

The graffiti beautifully depicted cherry blossoms in full bloom abutting a duck pond guarding a small cemetery. ARC9 studied the text on the headstones: 100 names, but only 99 dates. The robot wondered if the scene celebrated Gable J’s life?
Sandy thought it a warning

Selective breeding was bad enough. Now genetic screening? Sandy scoffed at the idea stubbornly insisting house dog clones would not be far behind.
ARC9 not comfortable with this line of inquiry, quickly changed the subject

A ribbon of ducks beat their way upriver to Lake Friend. From there, guided by a street dog and his robot companion, the ducks would portage through Summer’s Notch, pick up the mighty Karl taking them safely south.
“Shall we begin?” chirped ARC9.
Sandy looked for salmon

Despite a soft upbringing- couches, blankets, organic food, Sandy felt Hunter a worthy trail mate. The house dog worshipped him, naturally,  was a quick study, and had a naïve fearlessness that came in handy when a decoy was required.
ARC9 could be a bit dry too

No oracle would have predicted what Sandy found inside ARC9’s chest cavity. A nesting bird! So that’s where all the chirping came from…
The robot remembered saving it from a storm. A habit apparently

ARC9 watched Sandy dream run for several minutes followed by lip licking and a look of conquest.  The street dog then took several deep breaths and slipped into a deep sleep of contentment.  Few pleasures rival dreams of beating house dogs to the grill

The governor's mantle hung limp behind the office desk, a coarse sign of his disappearance. Although no ransom note had been found, kidnapping rumors were mounting. ARC9 and Sandy took note his house dog was also missing. That trail would be easier to follow

Sandy lamented the increased case load had lead to a shift from relaxing to working on the weekends.  He liked being busy, but did also like taking naps. ARC9 noted criminals seemed to work on the weekends too

The parade brought Sandy and ARC9 back to the pier and tantalizing amusement park. Sandy drooled through the fence at The Raptor's gravity defying loop-to-loop.
 "I'll ask again"
But the street dog had already retuned to the boardwalk's food trucks.
The dream was enough

The graffiti wall at the city boathouse gave evidence the governor’s disappearance may have been voluntary. Not the beautiful pictures that mesmerized ARC9, nor the crude language, but the p-mail. Sandy sniffed the governor’s dog excitedly bragging “and we’re outta here”

ARC9 carefully scanned the steep dew coated steps leading to the floating docks; eventually concluding the job required four paws.
Down Sandy scampered, finding the governor's sloop empty at its mooring. House dog scent, however, painted Misty B's vacant zodiac berth

ARC9 located Misty B's boat adrift in a constellation of islands south of the mainland. The robot landed the sea-plane next to the boat; Sandy boarding starboard fore, working aft. No sign of either missing human could be found. A house dog was quite relieved, however

Sandy had stopped listening to the governor’s dog— all the thank yous, the drama… it was too much. The house dog was not going to starve and isolation is good for dogs. Helps clear the mind.
ARC9 needed help clearing the sea-plane; to make room for the new passenger

Sandy was getting tired. ARC9 had steamed Elf and Christmas Vacation and had started in on the street dog’s favorite but it was getting late. Mclane and Gruber had not yet started to tussle when Sandy let out a yawn. Did the robot have a pause button?

Sandy was the second string shortstop for the North Beach kickball team. He would have been the starter but he did not always show up for practice, and that mattered optically.  ARC9 was third string catcher. Though the robot was primarily used as score board

With clouds parting, Sandy headed over to the resort pool hoping to take in a vacation day in style. He needed ARC9, though; the street dog could not inflate the plastic pineapple float himself. Something about opposable thumbs.

Where was the robot? The arcade perhaps?

Convincing the governor’s niece to talk would take logic and charm. The constable wielded neither.  Fortunately he had brought ARC9 and Sandy as backup.

Alas she was a cat person.

“Good day young lady” chirped the robot.
Logically, Sandy tried to look aloof

Fog evaporated any chance of following the thieves’ footprints through the lowlands. Even ARC9’s scanner was no use. When the constantable turned back Sandy barked and with a confident sniff assured them he could guide the search.
The thieves had stolen pie after all

Sandy positioned himself between the constable and the governor’s niece; ears up, tail down. ARC9 had not anticipated conflagration risk, but the street dog’s instinct should not be questioned. Everyone waited.

The robot blinked first ironically asking “who is hungry?”

Felicity's foul mood improved not from the constable's platitudes nor ARC9's dulcet singing. No, her enemy was Sandy's big eyes and obvious plea to play fetch on the beach. As the street dog's wet nose nudged her towards the door a smile emerged. Sandy had his ways

The High St farmers market had no CC-TVs, making Sunday prime time for illicit transactions. ARC9 took note of those giving sideways glances; Sandy hobnobbed with the country dogs. In the end neither learned much of the governor or his mistress, but they did acquire pie

At the tick of midnight, Sandy mysteriously sat up, fast asleep. Lifting his nose, he then launched a barrage of dream-howls at the moon- not wolf like, but a high static rumble.
A murder of crows looked on.
ARC9 understood. The street dog often dreamed of space travel

Suzy sat squarely on ARC9’s lap, the red cloth softening the robot’s metallic legs.
 “Are you really santa, or a robot in disguise?”
Sandy gave a cautioning glance.
 “And aren’t you a little small for a reindeer?”

“Citizens will obey the evacuation order Constable, not because of your badge, but because it’s the logical choice”
The constable smiled at ARC9’s optimism.
Taking matters into his own hand, Sandy began to run the beach barking loudly. Waves were already gaining height

For dogs with exceptional hearing quiet is a present. For some an uncomfortable present but not Sandy who had spent enough time in the country. He relished it.

ARC9 with exceptional noise canceling circuits delivered it.

The street dog soundly slept dreaming of stars

“…and the sheep dog found the manger hay soft and comforting…”
Sandy appreciated ARC9 would include the dogs in the retelling of holiday origin stories.  The robot did not always get the breed right, but Sandy found no reason to correct him

Sandy eagerly watched ARC9 open the street dog's present: a new drone, hopefully useful in their rescue cases. A flashback to last year's holiday, and an angry miliner, however, made the robot nervous.
Sandy wagged. He'd made a deal with the Constable. ARC9 was chirpless
